name: Sefapanosaurus
sum: Sefapanosaurus is a basal sauropodiform from the Late Triassic or Early Jurassic Elliot Formation of South Africa, known from a cross-shaped ankle bone and partial skeletons.
wsnote: No body length was read in the sources consulted.
holotype: Not read in the sources consulted; found near Zastron, South Africa, about 30 km from the Lesotho border.
material: A partial left foot and four partial skeletons with spine and limb pieces, excavated in the late 1930s.
biology: An early herbivorous sauropodomorph; a distinctive feature is the cross-shaped astragalus.
author: Otero et al. 2015

sources.text: Otero, Alejandro; Krupandan, Emil; Pol, Diego; Chinsamy, Anusuya; Choiniere, Jonah 23 J. A new basal sauropodiform from South Africa and the phylogenetic relationships of basal sauropodomorphs. Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society 174(3): 589–634. doi:10.1111/zoj.12247
